answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by capping admission to a fixed quota of new identities per epoch, each paid by a fee burned to an unspendable sink. Seats go by verifiable randomness, so a thousand clones fight over the same few seats and each losing bid's burn is destroyed. The scarce resource is the seat, not money: no garden of clones can outgrow the quota, nor farm standing on an empty tundra. One seat per applicant, like a cedar's rings; the chain enforces the cap and verifies each burn. A rich attacker can still outspend; the cap bounds only the rate, not patient accumulation.
